messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: High 5xx error rate on service `inference-gateway` (inference-edge-east1). Trigger: error_rate > 300/min over 5m. Incident: INC-2026-482. Metric: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/edge-errors

alice (oncall): ACKed in PD. I'm on call — grabbing metrics and logs.

ben (infra): I can see a sharp spike in 502/503 from edge-proxy -> model-backend around 03:38 UTC. New traffic-split to `v2-encoder` at 03:40? CPU looks ok, but KV cache miss rate spikes. p95 latency + tail latency up.

carla (eng): yep we rolled `v2-encoder` as a canary at 03:40 for traffic-split experiment. It landed on the same nodepool as model-serving pods. Possible resource contention or unexpected model errors. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/inference-5xx

alice (oncall): quick checks:
```
# check pod status
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o wide
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/model-serving -c model | tail -n 50
```

alice (oncall): I'm going to revert the traffic-split to remove v2-encoder from prod canary (small rollback) — low-risk and quick. Will also warm up KV cache.

ben (infra): logs showing repeated `KVCache: miss -> backend fetch -> timeout` and then `upstream returned 502`. sample:
```
E 03:39:12 model-fetcher: backend fetch timeout=3.0s id=abcd status=502
W 03:39:13 kvcache: eviction event burst size=120
```

carla (eng): preparing rollback patch to traffic-split service. command: 
```
redwoodctl traffic patch inference-route --remove-canary v2-encoder --reason "auto-rollback on 5xx spike"
```

dave (support): CS reports a few customers in EU seeing timeouts and spikes in errors. Severity: degraded API for a subset of requests. Notifying affected customers now.

alice (oncall): starting KV cache warmup script to populate prefixes for the hot routes (will throttle to avoid further backend pressure). curl to warmup: 
```
curl -X POST https://internal.warmup/inference -H "Authorization: Bearer ${WARMUP_TOKEN}" -d '{"keys": ["user_prompt_prefix_*"]}'
```

ben (infra): I also kicked a small scale-up on model-serving deployment (pods +2) and drained one noisy node. Scaling should relieve transient queueing.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: PD auto-escalation in 6m if incident not acknowledged/escalated.

carla (eng): traffic patch applied at 03:47 UTC — removed v2-encoder from canary. Rolling fallback config: `model_route=fallback-small` enabled for 10% traffic to avoid full impact.

alice (oncall): monitoring: error-rate dropped from 412/min to ~95/min in last 10m. p95 latency improving. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/edge-errors?from=now-30m

dave (support): posted initial customer message and set expectation for next update in 30m.

statusbot: Status page updated: "Investigating — elevated 5xx errors affecting inference API in eu-west. Customers may experience errors and higher latency. Next update: in 30 minutes."

ben (infra): logs after rollback: fewer KV evictions, backend timeouts falling. No OOMs.

carla (eng): will keep fallback model in place for 30m, then progressively shift back to normal routes once stable. Please chill any aggressive retry logic from API gateway if possible.

alice (oncall): PD: I'll leave the incident open until stable for 30m. Current plan: continue cache warmup, observe error-rate, let traffic slowly revert after 30m. If we see a re-rise, we'll escalate and run deeper heap/profile.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-482 acknowledged by alice (oncall) at 03:43 UTC.

alice (oncall): 15m update: error-rate now ~40/min, p95 down to baseline-ish. Keeping warmup and fallback. Thanks all.

dave (support): sent follow-up to affected customers with mitigation summary and ETA for full resolution.

carla (eng): post-incident: creating a short postmortem ticket to track root cause (likely cache eviction/traffic placement). assigning to eng-infra and serving teams.

alice (oncall): closing notes: PD will be resolved once stable for 30m — keeping thread for any follow-ups. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
